title: Inkwell performance tile: compact per-model & per-route telemetry spec
creator: Ava Martinez
summary: Design a compact, reusable performance tile (the 'Inkwell') for Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route telemetry (latency quantiles, throughput, token metrics, and cost overlays) for both overview grids and expanded detail panes.
design_goals: Enable rapid scanning: show p50/p95/p99 latency, current RPS, avg tokens/request, and token-cost estimate in one glance
Responsive and embeddable: tile must work in dense lists (8 per row) and expanded model pages
Actionable drilldowns: click-through to timeline, request-sampler, and rollout controls
Cost-awareness: provide token-cost overlay and delta to baseline model (savings/overage)
Low-noise visualization: prioritize compact glyphs and microcharts for noisy metrics
user_stories: As an on-call engineer, I want to see p95 latency and recent spike indicators so I can quickly determine if a model route is straining SLOs.
As a product manager, I want cost-per-1k-tokens shown with trend so I can spot regressions after a rollout.
As a platform engineer, I want a one-click path from tile to route rollout controls to initiate fallback when latency exceeds thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Tile displays p50/p95/p99 latency numerically and as a small quantile ribbon
Tile includes a micro-sparkline for 15m latency trend and a small throughput (RPS) badge
Token metrics shown: avg tokens/request and 24h token-volume; cost overlay opens detailed cost modal
Clicking tile header opens expanded detail pane with full charts (distribution violin, request waterfall, tokens-by-endpoint), and preserves filter context
Accessible to keyboard and screen readers: labels and aria descriptors provided for all microcharts
Design handoff includes color tokens, spacing scale, and responsive breakpoints
variants: Compact grid tile (60–90px height) for high-density overview
Medium tile (140px height) with two-line summary and medium sparkline for team dashboards
Expanded panel (full route page) with large distribution and interactive timeline
Alert state variant showing amber/red stripe + inline mitigation CTA
chart_specifications: Quantile ribbon (mini): horizontal bar showing p50/p75/p95 using layered opacity; width maps to latency; color uses semantic latency token
Sparkline (trend): 15m rolling median sampled at 1m cadence; hover reveals tooltip with exact numeric and timestamp
Throughput badge: numeric RPS with delta compared to previous window; uses up/down caret and micro-color
Latency distribution (expanded): violin plot + boxplot overlay; show sample density, median line, and p99 marker; allow log-scale toggle
Request waterfall (expanded): stacked microbars representing tokenization, model forward, IO, and network; each stack annotated with avg ms and % of total
Token cost overlay: translucent ribbon across charts showing cost per-1k tokens; hover shows cost breakdown by model variant and quantization profile
Anomaly spark (mini): small dot above ribbon when anomaly detector flags traffic deviation; click opens sampler view
widget_layout: Grid column span: compact tile = 1 col; medium = 2 cols; expanded = full-width
Left side: headline label (model/route) + status dot + dropdown for quick actions
Center: quantile ribbon stacked above sparkline
Right side: numeric badges for p95, RPS, avg tokens, cost-per-1k
Footer: micro-actions (open details, open rollout, pin to dashboard)
interaction_notes: Hover on quantile ribbon shows p50/p95/p99 numeric callouts; keyboard focus exposes same callouts
Clicking cost badge opens cost modal anchored to tile with deep links to billing dashboard
Context menu (three-dot) contains: Export sample, Open in logs, Create alert from metric
Drag-and-drop tiles to rearrange on custom dashboards; snap-to-grid with animation
When a route is in canary rollout, an overlay badge shows percentage of traffic and a mini-sparkline comparing baseline vs canary latency
accessibility_considerations: All color-coded metrics must include textual fallback (e.g., 'p95: 230 ms')
Contrast ratios for latency states meet AA for normal text; icons include aria-labels
Keyboard order flows: header actions -> main chart -> badges -> footer actions
Tooltips remain visible to keyboard users; long descriptions added for violin plots in aria-describedby
